data.narrative:
Lightmatter is a Series C semiconductor company that has raised $420M+ to date, operating within a competitive frontier-chip sector anchored by 8 private peers and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD). The private peer set spans stages from Series B through Series D, with valuations ranging from $529M to $2.7B.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base, applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $714M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), Nearfield Instruments ($1.6B, Series D), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—produces a $1.3B median. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 20.4x across three semiconductors tickers) is not applicable due to absence of target revenue disclosure, typical for private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $607M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $1.0B. This range reflects meaningful divergence between stage-based and peer-relative methods, driven primarily by stage heterogeneity within the peer set and reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy. Key uncertainties include Lightmatter's revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peers, and technology differentiation within an increasingly crowded semiconductor subsector.
